data.title: Anthropic Stock Is Attracting Over $1 Billion in Retail Trading. Here's What's Happening
data.description:
Retail investors rushed to trade shares of Claude AI developer Anthropic (ANT) on Thursday, with their total first-day trading activity projected to reach a record $1.4 billion. According to Bloomberg, Vanda Research expects individual investors to purchase a net $80 million to $90 million worth of shares, which would make Anthropic's debut the third-biggest IPO trading day for retail inflows. The activity followed Anthropic's $111.50 opening price, which was 34.3% above its $83 IPO price.

The difference between those figures is important. Net buying measures how much investors purchase after accounting for sales, while trading turnover includes both purchases and sales. Therefore, the projected $1.4 billion in turnover suggests that investors are actively trading Anthropic rather than simply buying shares to hold.

Vanda recorded $18.6 million in net retail purchases during Anthropic's first 30 minutes of trading. That was lower than expected, as the research firm had previously projected $250 million in first-day net purchases.

Even so, the updated $80 million to $90 million estimate would trail only space company SpaceX (SPCX), which attracted $118 million in June 2026, and cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase (COIN), which recorded $92 million in 2021.

Anthropic's Debut Draws Money Away From Other AI Stocks

However, some of the money entering Anthropic appears to be coming from existing AI investments. Vanda strategist Viraj Patel reported that retail traders were selling other AI stocks to fund their Anthropic purchases. Chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) was among the companies experiencing selling pressure, although its shares also fell after short-selling firm Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a bearish position and questioned the company's business ties to China.

Meanwhile, Patel said that buying interest in AI chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA), another popular stock among individual investors, had fallen.

Anthropic's record IPO also attracted demand from investors who wanted more shares than they received. According to The Wall Street Journal, retail investors received about 15% of the $81.34 billion public offering, compared with the maximum 20% allocation previously discussed.

Steven Quirk, chief brokerage officer at trading platform Robinhood Markets (HOOD), told Bloomberg that its customers wanted considerably more Anthropic shares than they received. However, every Robinhood customer who requested shares received at least one.

data.title: Skydance Stock (NYSE:SKYD) Down Over 5% as it Bows Out of World Cup Rights
data.description:
The bidding for World Cup rights apparently got too rich for the blood of entertainment giant Skydance (SKYD), as it pulled out of the bidding, according to a report from Bloomberg. This actually makes a certain amount of sense, especially given Skydance's post-merger priorities, but it will still likely hurt some viewers. Skydance stock dropped over 5% in the closing minutes of Thursday's trading. Skydance has seen a 57.14% loss in its share price over the past year.

We Have Soccer at Home

It might seem like a bad idea for Skydance to bow out of the bidding for the World Cup. The tournaments are supposed to bring in as much as $4 billion, with reports suggesting that $2 billion of that will come from the 2030 round while another $1 billion to $1.5 billion will come in for 2034. But Skydance's co-chief executive officer, David Ellison, made it clear that Skydance was going to be "disciplined" when it came to buying future sports media.

Given that Skydance owes somewhere in the neighborhood of $80 billion in debt outstanding since the merger, it makes sense that it would not want to shell out another $4 billion on top of that for a sporting event. Granted, that sporting event would have brought in quite a bit in ad revenue, but it's still a lot of money given what Skydance currently owes. Worse yet, the 2034 round of World Cup play will take place in Saudi Arabia, the report noted, and that represents a time zone issue that might be tougher for American audiences to get behind.

A New Bit of Science Fiction

Meanwhile, Skydance's David Ellison is taking something of a personal hand in a major, $100 million project that recently signed Chris Pratt to its cast list, noted a report from Page Six Hollywood. The movie is called The Traveler, and focuses on time travel, which apparently is enough to get Ellison himself interested.

The Traveler took on a bit of cachet in 2019, when it showed up on the Black List, an annual list that focused on unproduced Hollywood projects. Based on a novel, it focuses on a time traveler who would rather not be traveling through time, as well as his son, who shares a bond with his father that is never quite broken, even across thousands of years. It is considered an "elevated" science fiction story, the report noted, which may give Skydance a means to get out from under Star Trek as its primary science fiction connection.

data.title: Stock Market Selloff Hits Every Sector as Consumer Stocks Lead Declines
data.description:
U.S. stocks sold off on Thursday afternoon, with all 11 major S&P 500 sectors declining as investors pulled back from riskier assets. The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) showed the smallest loss at 0.55%, while the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY) fell by 2.29%. The selloff followed an early rally that was fueled by AI developer Anthropic's (ANT) stock market debut. However, enthusiasm faded as investors continued to assess the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook.

Minutes from the Fed's October meeting, released on Wednesday, showed that nearly all officials expected further rate increases if the economy performed as projected. Higher borrowing costs can discourage consumers from making expensive purchases, which adds pressure to businesses that depend on discretionary spending.

Meanwhile, the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV) declined by 1.98%, making it the second-worst-performing sector. The Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC) followed with a 1.85% loss.

Why Energy Stocks Are Holding Up Better Than Other Sectors

Energy's relative strength came as oil prices recovered from Wednesday's losses. According to Reuters, fresh reports of tanker disruptions near the Strait of Hormuz supported crude prices despite concerns about excess global supply. However, the recovery was limited by Wednesday's U.S. inventory report, which showed that crude stockpiles increased by 3.4 million barrels.

Elsewhere, the Industrial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLI) dropped by 1.61%, while the Materials Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLB) fell by 1.67%. These declines came as concerns about higher interest rates weighed on expectations for economic activity.

Even traditionally defensive sectors struggled. The Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLU) declined by 1.07%, while the Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLP) lost 1.33%.

Meanwhile, the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) fell by 1.27% despite the earlier AI-driven rally. The Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) slipped by 1.30%, while the Real Estate Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLRE) declined by 1.28%.

The bond market also showed signs of caution. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield stood near 5.05%, while the CBOE Volatility Index had climbed by 13.8% to 27.95.

Turning to Wall Street, TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), which tracks the overall stock market in the U.S. This is based on 415 Buys, 82 Holds, and six Sells assigned in the past three months. data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Gets Upgrade at DZ Bank, Share Prices Slip
data.description:
Normally, having an analyst say something good about your stock gives it a boost. This is not always the case, however, as legacy automaker Ford (F) found out to its dismay. Ford stock got a boost in ratings, but not in share price, as shares slipped fractionally in Thursday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen a 12.56% loss in its share price over the past year.

A Slightly Backhanded Upgrade

It did not help matters that the upgrade came with a cut in the price target. DZ Bank analyst Matthias Volkert upgraded Ford stock from Hold to Buy, but trimmed his price target to $15 a share from its original $16. A report from Barron's did not help matters much as they had not spotted a copy of Volkert's report that would indicate why he made these changes.

In general, however, there were some points that may have been weighing on investors' minds when it comes to Ford. Specifically there are concerns that 2027 will not live up to what 2026 looked like as interest rates continue to rise, inflation continues to impact customers, and even used car prices continue to look like a slightly erroneous phone number. However ,considering that Ford was trading over six times valuation earlier this year, but currently trades at about four times, that drop may have been enough for Volcker to encourage investors to get off the sidelines.

What's In the Box?

A report from Ford Authority brought in some extra interest, as a giant shipping container featuring the Ford Racing logo and the legend "Go Like Hell" recently emerged outside the World Headquarters building. Few are aware of what actually is in the shipping container, and Ford does not seem to be talking right now. However, the report suggests that it contains the new Ford hypercar, set to make its debut in the 2027 FIA World Endurance Championship season.

The shipping container's president presence would be an enigma alone for anyone, but Ford Authority also supplemented it with a bit of footage from an Instagram account. Given that the new Ford hypercar is supposed to be debuting on Thanksgiving Day this year, that may indeed be what it is. As for the phrase "go like hell," that refers to a remark written by Carroll Shelby during the 1966 running of the 24 Hours of Le Mans, which told Ken Miles to move past the 7,000 RPM mark in order to get a victory.

data.title: Why Is Penny Stock VivoSim Labs (VIVS) Up 120% Today?
data.description:
VivoSim Labs (VIVS) stock rocketed higher on Thursday after the pharmaceutical and biotechnology services company announced a new agreement. According to the company, it has reached a seven-figure agreement with a top-10 global pharmaceutical company. The company didn't reveal the exact size of this agreement or who it was with.

VivoSim Labs said that the customer intends to purchase its NAMkind testing services. The company's models have shown the ability to predict drug-induced liver injury with 91% accuracy, 90% sensitivity and 95% specificity. VivoSim Labs noted that this sale will push its revenue beyond the more than 500% growth outlook that it issued on July 15, 2026.

"In July we told shareholders revenue would grow more than 500% this fiscal year. The quarterly report we filed last week shows both toxicology businesses growing, and this agreement on its own is expected to take us past that number," said Keith Murphy, Executive Chairman of VivoSim Labs. "What matters more is what comes after it. A top-10 company has gone from evaluating our human liver and intestine models to paying for program work, and we expect its regular testing to follow. Other large customers are moving the same way."

VivoSim Labs said that the agreement will affect its earnings across several quarters. Specifically, investors will see the effect of this sale in the company's fiscal Q3 and Q4, ending Dec. 31 and March 31, respectively.

How This News Affected VIVS Stock

VivoSim Labs stock experienced a 119.8% rally on Thursday after the company announced the seven-figure deal, but the shares were still down 93.37% year-to-date. Investors will note that the stock has also fallen 94.39% over the past 12 months.

With today's news of a massive deal with a large customer came heavy trading of VIVS stock, as more than 573 million shares changed hands. To put that in perspective, the company's three-month average daily trading volume was about 1.06 million shares.

data.title: Oil Prices Climb on Alleged Strait of Hormuz Tanker Blasts Despite Signs of a Global Crude Surplus
data.description:
Oil prices climbed higher on Thursday as alleged tanker blasts in the Strait of Hormuz outweighed growing signs of a global crude surplus.

Brent crude (CM:BZ) rose 1.04%, or $0.96, to $93.62 a barrel on Thursday afternoon, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (CM:CL) crude gained 1.57%, or $1.30, to $84.47. Even with Thursday's bounce, Brent remains down 16.45% over the past month and U.S. crude sits 16.23% lower as recovering Gulf exports ease earlier supply fears.

Macroeconomic headwinds also kept rallies in check. Persistent U.S. inflation and expectations for a December Federal Reserve interest rate hike kept the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) near a 19-month high at 103.81 on Thursday. This makes dollar-priced oil costlier for overseas buyers.

Hormuz Tanker Blasts Have Lifted Crude Benchmarks

New shipping threats drove Thursday's price gains. Iran's navy stated via state media on Thursday that two oil tankers hit naval mines and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz, though the account has not been independently verified.

Energy traders also stayed cautious as Washington weighed more strikes on Iran after U.S. warplanes hit an Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island earlier this week. These security risks have delayed QatarEnergy's 2027 long-term crude supply talks with refiners, while Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. offered more term barrels to traders for next year, Bloomberg reported.

World Leaders Have Pledged Higher Fuel Supplies

High-level diplomacy pulled oil prices in the opposite direction on Thursday. At a three-way summit in China, U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged to expand refined fuel supplies for all countries, according to a joint statement released by the White House.

Separately on Thursday, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Washington is considering sending more crude and diesel to Europe, where the U.S. has become the top supplier during the Iran conflict, Reuters reported.

Still, Putin ruled out a Black Sea or energy truce with Ukraine on Thursday following a strike on the Crimea bridge, keeping risks over Russian diesel output alive.

Rising Inventories Cap Further Oil Price Gains

New supply figures reinforced expectations that the global oil market is moving back into surplus. Joint Organizations Data Initiative data released Thursday showed Saudi Arabia's crude exports jumped nearly 21% in September to 5.38 million barrels per day, reaching an eight-month high.

In the U.S., Energy Information Administration figures for the week ended November 13 showed commercial crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels, while gasoline stocks climbed past 5 million barrels, beating analyst forecasts.

Another 40 million barrels from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve are also scheduled to reach the market across November and December.

IEA Report Forecasts Looser Oil Markets

Longer-term forecasts released Thursday pointed to lower energy prices ahead once Middle East shipping recovers. In its flagship World Energy Outlook 2026 published Thursday, the International Energy Agency (IEA) reported that Hormuz disruptions removed 2.8 billion barrels of Middle East oil through October.

High fuel costs are expected to cut global oil demand by 2.7 million barrels per day in 2026 to 102.3 million barrels per day, marking the first annual drop since 2020.

Meanwhile, higher Gulf shipments lifted global supply to 105.4 million barrels per day in October, pushing supply back above demand.

"The pressures of the current crisis must not obscure the choices that will shape energy security, sustainability and prosperity for the decades to come," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said in Thursday's release.

Wood Mackenzie also cut its price forecast on Thursday, projecting Brent will drop to an average of $84 a barrel in 2027 and $55 in 2028 if a U.S.-Iran peace deal restores Gulf shipping flows.
data.author: Annika Masrani

data.title: Anthropic Stock Opens 34% Higher as Early Nasdaq Rally Fades
data.description:
U.S. stocks turned red on Thursday as excitement over the market debut of Claude AI developer Anthropic (ANT) failed to sustain an early rally. Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 on the Nasdaq (NDAQ), up 34.3% from their $83 initial public offering (IPO) price. At the time of writing, the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) was down 1.2%, while the S&P 500 fell 1.3%. In addition, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 2%.

Anthropic's strong debut comes after higher-than-expected demand for its IPO. The company and its selling shareholders offered 980 million shares at $83 each, above the original $70 to $78 range. That brought the public offering's value to $81.34 billion, which surpassed the $75 billion initially raised in space exploration company SpaceX's (SPCX) June IPO. Roughly $79.4 billion of Anthropic's offering proceeds went to the company itself before expenses.

However, gains in AI-related stocks started fading as other parts of the market weakened. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) initially climbed by 7.8% before its gain narrowed to 1.5%. AI cloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV) also gave up most of an earlier 10.5% jump.

Intel's Chipmaking Deal Adds to AI Stock Moves

Elsewhere, chipmaker Intel (INTC) is up after CEO Lip-Bu Tan announced the firm's first outside customer for its advanced 18A manufacturing technology. Intel later confirmed that the unnamed customer chose its improved 18A-P process, which entered risk production in June. The agreement gives Intel an early customer as it tries to attract more companies to its contract chipmaking business.

Cybersecurity provider Palo Alto Networks (PANW) also gained after reporting better-than-expected quarterly results and agreeing to buy Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock. The acquisition would help Palo Alto offer secure AI services to business customers.

Meanwhile, retailer Walmart (WMT) fell despite raising its Fiscal 2027 outlook. Quarterly revenue grew by 5.2% to $188.8 billion, while global e-commerce sales increased by 17%.

Oil prices also climbed as reports of tanker disruptions near the Strait of Hormuz added supply concerns. Brent crude rose 1% to $93.56 per barrel, while U.S. crude futures rose 1.3% to $84.24. The rebound comes after Wednesday's losses, when U.S. crude inventories increased by 3.4 million barrels.

data.title: VOO vs. DRAM: AI Chip Bet or Broad Market — Which ETF Wins?
data.description:
Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) and Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) offer very different ways to invest in the stock market. While VOO tracks the S&P 500, DRAM gives investors direct exposure to memory chip stocks. Using TipRanks' ETF Comparison Tool, we compared VOO and DRAM to find the best ETF for investors.

VOO vs. DRAM: Which ETF Holdings Offer the Most Upside?

According to TipRanks' unique ETF Analyst Consensus, which is based on a weighted average of analyst ratings for each ETF's holdings, VOO has a Moderate Buy rating.

VOO has an average price target of $844.70, implying 24.83% upside. Among its holdings, SanDisk (SNDK)  has the highest upside potential at 160%, followed by Micron (MU) at 118%.

DRAM's top holdings by upside potential include Kioxia Holdings Corporation (JP:285A) at 372% and SanDisk at 160%.

DRAM or VOO – Key Differences

VOO is much cheaper to own than DRAM. It charges an annual fee of just 0.03%, or $3 for every $10,000 invested. DRAM charges 0.65%, which works out to $65 a year on the same investment. DRAM's higher fee reflects its focus on memory chip stocks. VOO is the cheaper option for long-term investors who want broad market exposure.

DRAM is much more concentrated than VOO. Its top 10 holdings make up 71.26% of the portfolio, compared with just 37% for VOO. This means DRAM is heavily exposed to a handful of companies. VOO spreads its money across hundreds of U.S. stocks.

DRAM also carries higher risk with a beta of 3.87, while VOO's beta is 1.00.

VOO and DRAM – Major Holdings

VOO holds 507 stocks with total assets worth $1.04 trillion. VOO's top 5 holdings are Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), and Alphabet (GOOGL).

DRAM ETF includes firms that make DRAM, HBM, NAND flash, and SSD technologies. DRAM owns 19 stocks, with major holdings such as SK Hynix (SKHY), Samsung (SSNLF), SanDisk, and Seagate (STX).

Conclusion

VOO is the safer, long-term option because it is broadly diversified and grows steadily across the whole U.S. market. On the other hand, DRAM is a higher-risk, higher-reward ETF focused on AI memory and semiconductors, so it can rise faster in strong chip cycles but also fall harder when the sector slows down.

data.title: Alphabet Stock (GOOGL) Ticks Up After Picking Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to Launch AI Satellites in 2029
data.description:
Alphabet (GOOGL) stock ticked up on Thursday morning after the search giant picked Amazon (AMZN) founder Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to launch AI computing satellites into orbit. The deal targets a first-quarter 2029 flight on Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, according to a Blue Origin press release.

The flight is part of Project Suncatcher, which is Google's plan to run AI chips on solar power in space so they do not strain electric grids and cooling systems on Earth. Neither company shared what the deal is worth.

Blue Origin Wins Deal to Launch Google's AI Satellites

Thursday's pact marks Google's first dedicated heavy-lift flight for Project Suncatcher. New Glenn can lift 45 metric tons to low Earth orbit inside a seven-meter nose cone, Unite.AI reported. Each satellite will carry Google's Tensor Processing Units with computing power roughly equal to one server rack in sun-synchronous orbit.

Jordan Charles, Senior Vice President of New Glenn at Blue Origin, said in the press release that the rocket's "heavy-lift capacity and large payload volume give customers the flexibility to bring new capabilities to orbit." The win follows a May 28 Cape Canaveral test explosion tied to a BE-4 engine valve that pushed New Glenn's next flight to January 2027.

Google Tests AI Chips in Orbit with Planet Labs

Google and Planet Labs (PL) launched a refrigerator-sized Project Suncatcher prototype on October 1 aboard a SpaceX (SPCX) rocket, according to Google's Project Suncatcher research blog.

On October 30, Google reported on its blog that the satellite's chip ran its Gemma 4 model in orbit and beamed back a short poem while passing over Norway. Engineers are checking how the chips handle space radiation and extreme heat released through heat pipes and radiator panels.

Furthermore, Google plans two linked test satellites in 2027 and has studied 81-satellite laser-linked clusters 650 kilometers above Earth.

Space Rivals Push for Orbital Data Centers Despite Large Costs

SpaceX (SPCX) and Nvidia (NVDA)-backed startup Starcloud are also working on space data centers. Starcloud raised $250 million at a $2.3 billion valuation in an August round led by Manhattan West with participation from Nvidia, according to Starcloud's press release.

Still, launch prices must drop from roughly $7,000 per kilogram today to around $200 per kilogram by the mid-2030s to match ground power costs, according to Google's Project Suncatcher research blog

Is Google Stock a Strong Buy Right Now?

Turning to the Street, Alphabet's stock (GOOGL) carries a Strong Buy consensus based on 30 Buy and four Hold ratings assigned in the past three months. The average 12-month GOOGL stock price target is $398.50, which implies 38% upside from the current price. (See GOOGL stock forecast)

data.title: Tech and AI Stocks Rise on Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut
data.description:
Technology and artificial intelligence (AI) stocks rose on Thursday morning as investors cheered the much-awaited Nasdaq debut of Claude AI maker Anthropic (ANT). Notably, Anthropic raised more money than expected, with its initial public offering (IPO) priced at $83 per share, above the initial $70-$78 target range. Anthropic also upsized its offering, selling 980 million shares to raise $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX's (SPCX) June 2026 IPO.

The Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 Index (SPX) rose 1.71% and 0.82%, respectively, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) was slightly down as of 10:07 a.m. EST on November 19.

Shares of neocloud companies and chip and AI-related stocks advanced as Anthropic's IPO lifted investor sentiment. AI stocks have been under pressure recently amid concerns about the sustainability of massive spending and steep valuations. Additionally, Intel (INTC) shares rose as CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the chipmaker has signed its first external customer for its 18A chips, CNBC reported. Pushkar Ranade, Intel's technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer signed up for Intel's 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June.

Also, Palo Alto (PANW) shares jumped after the cybersecurity company reported solid Q1 FY27 results and announced the $4.5 billion acquisition of Applied Compute. However, Walmart (WMT) stock fell despite the big-box retailer raising its full-year outlook, driven by strength in e-commerce sales.

Meanwhile, oil prices rose on Thursday morning after falling in the previous session. Rising global oil supply and higher U.S. interest rates are limiting gains, while persistent geopolitical risks in the Middle East are supporting higher prices. At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 1.46% to $93.29 per barrel, while WTI crude futures rose 1.61% to $84.60 per barrel.

During Wednesday's regular trading session, the three major U.S. indexes closed mixed. The Dow Jones and the S&P 500 fell 1.11% and 0.23%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.42%.
